title: Attention Gardens — field notes on sparsity, KV compression, and long-context heuristics
body:
Quick intro / context:
I want a compact, runnable mental model for how attention sparsity techniques and KV-compression interact with real-serving constraints (latency SLOs, memory on 80GB A100, cost per token). These are first-pass notes + a short experiment plan to validate hypotheses. Keep rough — capture intuition and concrete signals we can measure.

Papers & takeaways (short):
- Sparse Sinkhorn / Routing attention (paper: 2024-ish): routing-based sparsity can reduce compute substantially for long contexts, but the dynamic routing step often becomes the new bottleneck unless fused with GPU kernels. Takeaway: sparsity is valuable only when the routing cost < saved attention compute for the typical sequence lengths in our workloads.
- FlashAttention 2 / kernel-fusion notes (FlashAttention repo link above): massive speedups for dense attention by kernel fusion and workspace reduction. For small batches and high seq len it's our baseline; any sparse variant must beat FA2 wall-clock for representative batch/seq distributions.
- KV compression / prefix distillation ideas: compressing prefix KV into compact summaries (PCA, product quantization on keys, learned summaries) saves memory but risks accuracy on retrieval-like tasks. Practical compromise: hybrid: keep high-precision for last N tokens (e.g., 2k) and compressed older KV.
- Mixture-of-experts for KV shards / routing: can shard KV across devices and route only to relevant experts. Complexity leaps because we need cross-device routing and backpressure control in the runtime.

Concrete experiments to run (priority order):
1) FlashAttention2 baseline microbenchmarks (batches: 1, 4, 16; seq lens: 512, 2048, 8192) on the small-team benchmark dataset. Measure: tokens/sec, p99 latency, GPU memory footprint. Add cost estimate (GPU-hours * $/hr).
2) Simple static sparsity mask (local window + strided): Implement as offline transformer inference using patched aten kernels (or use our prototype sparse kernel) and measure same dims as baseline. Key signal: where does p99 blow up? Routing overhead vs. attention compute saved.
3) KV-compression probe: pipeline where we store prefix KV in 8-bit PQ vectors, keep last 2k tokens in fp16. Run retrieval+generation prompts and compute ROUGE/BLEU-ish proxies + embedding-similarity drop. Metric: delta in generation score vs baseline and memory saved.
4) End-to-end simulated serving test: inject compressed-KV + sparse attention into the runtime shim (non-optimized) and measure latency tail for a synthetic mix (50% short chat, 30% medium batch, 20% long context). Look for error modes: slow routing, desync on cache hits, cold-start penalty.

Hypotheses (to validate):
- H1: For seq len < 2k, FA2 dense attention is still the fastest; sparsity only pays off consistently for >4k with batch sizes <= 8.
- H2: Mixed-precision KV (hot region fp16, cold region PQ8) yields >30% memory reduction with <2% generation quality degradation on retrieval-augmented prompts if PQ is trained on in-domain keys.
- H3: Routing-based sparse attention without fused kernels increases p99 more than it reduces average compute unless we co-design routing to be low-branching (top-k per query <= 8).

Notes on measurement design (practical):
- Use our existing microbench harness (RINF-4021) and add an 'attention-flavors' axis: {dense-fa2, window+strided, routing, routing+fused} and a 'kv-storage' axis: {fp16-all, hot-cold-pq, full-pq}.
- Record token-level traces for 1k requests to inspect where spikes happen. Collect GPU profiler traces for candidate slow cases.
- Use synthetic + sampled real workloads. Synthetic to exercise extremes, sampled for real mix.

Implementation roughs and gotchas: 
- Kernel availability: if fused routing kernels aren't in our stack, emulate but expect p99 inflation. Consider partnering with infra to test on next-gen drivers.
- Memory fragmentation: compressed KV introduces non-uniform allocation patterns; SRE warnings possible. Track internal OOM and fragmentation metrics.
- Determinism/seed issues: PQ-based decompression can be non-deterministic if not careful with rounding. Repro seeds for eval runs.

Questions & open decisions:
- What in-domain data should we train PQ on? Candidate: a 1M-token sample across hosted-api chat logs (anonymized) + wiki crawl. Need privacy sign-off for hosted logs.
- Where to place prototypes? dev-gpu-03 (80GB) or a smaller dedicated cluster? For routing fusion tests we may need multi-GPU.
- Beam/decoder interaction: compressed KV may skew top-k probabilities for beam search — track sample diversity.

Short reading list (to prioritize):
- FlashAttention 2 paper + repo (high priority)
- "Routing Transformers" and follow-ups (survey)
- PQ / IVF product quantization primers + faiss examples (notes below)
- Any Redwood internal notes on prefix caching and rollout experiments (link to Jira above)

Experiment timeline (2-week sprint):
- Day 1–2: FA2 baseline and harness parameterization.
- Day 3–6: Implement static sparsity masks + run microbench.
- Day 7–10: KV compression prototype + offline accuracy checks.
- Day 11–12: Combined runtime sim and p99 analysis.
- Day 13–14: Triage, capture write-up, and propose next step (move to Dedicated test cluster or stop).

Slack/PR/Confluence hooks to create:
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/pull/xxx - add attention-flavors axis
- Confluence page: "attention-gardens-experiments" (initial notes + results)
- Slack thread: #eng-inference -> pin perf traces and final remarks

Decision criteria for next step (stop vs escalate):
- If memory savings >25% with <=1.5% quality drop AND p99 < 1.5x baseline, escalate to Dedicated cluster tests.
- If p99 > 2x baseline or quality drop >3%, deprioritize and document failure modes.

Quick TODOs (myself):
- [ ] Draft PQ training script (small sample) — target by 2026-06-06.
- [ ] Add FA2 configs to harness and run seq=4096 test on dev-gpu-03.
- [ ] Sync with Maya on in-domain corpus selection and privacy consent.

Random heuristics and heuristics-to-try (brain-dump):
- When compressing KV, preserve norm information (scale per-key) separately to help decoder attention weighting.
- Prefer block-PQ (blocks of 64 dims) instead of global PQ to reduce quantization bleed for local features.
- Warm-start PQ centroids from k-means on a small prefix set rather than random init.

Notes-to-self: keep these notes informal; once experiments land, convert to a proper doc under shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml and link results.

End of file.
